summary.headline: Stylam Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin crossed 20%, with management guiding 19-20%+ going forward and the third plant targeted for commercial production by early September.
summary.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 margins beat the company's usual ~20% ceiling, which they attributed to higher utilisation and sales volume rather than inventory gains. The new third laminate plant has slipped from earlier timelines; dry run is under way and management targets commercial production around 15-20 August, with 1 September as the outer limit. Domestic revenue remains flat with restructuring (new team, distributors, warehouses) guided to show results from Q3 FY27. Management said the next major capex announcement is deferred to after the plant starts, around the end of August or early September.

segments.name: Laminates (exports)
segments.commentary: Europe is the strongest export region per management; US and Middle East each estimated at 10-15% of laminate revenue. Laminate capacity has a 5-10% efficiency gap to close.

segments.name: Laminates (domestic)
segments.commentary: Domestic sales stuck around INR300 crore run rate for four years per analyst. Price hikes taken across multiple SKUs, but volumes flat; restructuring to add distributors, warehouses and states.

segments.name: Acrylic
segments.commentary: Acrylic capacity is completely empty per management; ties to the domestic and export revamp. Aica may begin taking acrylic, but management said this is unconfirmed (3-4 months to know).

segments.name: Third plant (new laminate plant)
segments.commentary: Management expects roughly INR250-300 crore revenue this fiscal at 25-30% first-year utilisation, ramping month on month with no annual POs. Commercial production targeted by 15-20 August, latest 1 September.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to stay around 19-20%+ even after the new plant starts.
Third plant: INR250-300 crore revenue expected this fiscal; 25-30% first-year utilisation (management said 30% ramp by year end, later 'conservative' framing).
Domestic volumes flat in Q1; ramp-up slow in Q2, significant from Q3 FY27.
Domestic revenue share expected to rise slowly from about 25%, with margins held steady.
Next major capex announcement deferred to after plant start (end-August/early-September); new capex to focus on domestic market and to avoid laminate saturation.
Raw material costs unchanged; price hikes to hold; reversal only if war-driven input costs fall, which may take 6-9 months.
capex_capacity: Third laminate plant: dry run under way; commercial production targeted 15-20 August, outer limit 1 September 2026; delay attributed to monsoon rain (1-2 months) and a family dispute that slowed work.
Laminate capacity at 5-10% efficiency headroom per management.
Next major capex to be announced after the new plant is running; management said it is evaluating options and may defer to next quarter.
Promoter holds about 17% after Aica's stake purchase; management said no plan to raise stake from open market for now.
demand_pricing: Price hikes taken in Q1 FY27 across multiple domestic product lines (1 mm, 0.8 mm, compact laminates), varying by SKU; no further hike planned for now.
Phenol around USD1,400/ton; melamine USD1,000-1,100/ton; kraft and deco paper costs unpredictable.
US tariff: management said 10%, with a reported re-implementation after a brief move to 0%.
Logistics costs high globally, especially for the Middle East.
Domestic restructuring: new team, distributors in new states, warehouses; previously present only in about four or five cities.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin spike above 20% and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no inventory gain; margins came from efficiency and higher utilisation as sales rose. They expect 19-20%+ to hold after the new plant starts.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the plant delayed and is the INR300 crore revenue still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays were due to a family dispute that slowed work and monsoon rain. Management still expects INR250-300 crore revenue from the plant this year, with commercial production by 15-20 August or 1 September at the latest.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Aica partnership and tech transfer scope?
qa_highlights.answer: Aica has joined the Board (first meeting 22 July); no operational role or export discussions yet. Tech transfer could cover any product, possibly over the next 3-4 months.

qa_highlights.question: How long until domestic revival and what is changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said results should show from Q3 FY27 after restructuring of the team, distributors and warehouses; Q1 volumes flat, Q2 slow ramp.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall about 10% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the Q4 base included an annual actuarial valuation booked in the audited year-end; Q1 has none. Management expects employee cost to stay at current levels post-commissioning.

risks_watch: Plant has slipped repeatedly since about November 2025; commercial production date (August/September) must be met to deliver INR250-300 crore FY27 revenue.
Raw material inflation tied to the West Asia conflict; price hikes may need reversal or further increases.
Domestic turnaround depends on restructuring that management says will show results only from Q3 FY27.
Governance and family dispute reference flagged by investors; Aica's board role and capex announcement timing still unclear.
Logistics and US tariff uncertainty (10% duty, reported re-implementation) for export markets.
Transcript audibility was poor for much of the call; some management answers and figures may be misheard, so verify against the audio or the company's filing before relying on them.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and the plant timeline, but defensive on domestic weakness and on the repeated delays, which management blamed on monsoon rain and a family dispute. Evasive on price hike percentages and on the next capex, which it deferred.
key_quotes: I think the margins will remain the same, that is why even when the new capex will start end of August.
No, no inventory gain. nothing. It is our efficiency and it is our more utilization and if you go for sales figures it is increased.
It will be on a month-on-month basis only. So, there is no POs in our industry that we get a PO for entire year.

Growth in low single digits per analyst; management says volumes flat vs Q4

financial_highlights.value: Declined about 10% QoQ (per analyst question; CFO cited actuarial valuation done annually in Q4, not in Q1)

adds.what: Third laminate plant, INR250-300 crore first-year revenue at 25-30% utilisation

growth.why: Management guides third plant to add INR250-300 crore revenue this fiscal at 25-30% first-year utilisation, with commercial production targeted 15-20 August (latest 1 September), but domestic volumes are flat until Q3 FY27 and no revenue growth % is guided.
